world.title: Australian MP Helen Haines begins rehabilitation after losing both legs
world.summary: Australian independent lawmaker Helen Haines left a Melbourne hospital on Monday to begin rehabilitation, four weeks after a vehicle struck her outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, causing injuries that required both legs to be amputated. The 65-year-old said rehabilitation would continue in Melbourne for the i
world.content: Australian independent lawmaker Helen Haines left a Melbourne hospital on Monday to begin rehabilitation, four weeks after a vehicle struck her outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, causing injuries that required both legs to be amputated. The 65-year-old said rehabilitation would continue in Melbourne for the immediate future. She thanked supporters and described the care she received at The Alfred hospital as expert and compassionate. Police have charged 43-year-old Brendan Nugent with dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury and the federal offence of harming a public official. He remains in custody. The investigation continues, and police have not established a motive. Nugent has yet to enter a plea, and his next court appearance is scheduled for February. Security was increased at several electorate offices after Haines was injured. Australian politicians have traditionally had relatively little security. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said he remained in regular contact with her and her family. Haines has not announced when she will resume parliamentary or constituency work.

world.title: Founder of Mexico’s Guadalajara Cartel dies in custody at 80
world.summary: Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo, founder of Mexico’s Guadalajara Cartel, died at 80 on Nov. 15 in a private hospital in Guadalajara, Jalisco, after suffering multiple organ failure, state authorities said. He had been transferred two days earlier from Puente Grande prison, where he had been held since 1989. A former police
world.content: Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo, founder of Mexico’s Guadalajara Cartel, died at 80 on Nov. 15 in a private hospital in Guadalajara, Jalisco, after suffering multiple organ failure, state authorities said. He had been transferred two days earlier from Puente Grande prison, where he had been held since 1989. A former police officer, Félix Gallardo helped build a trafficking network that linked Mexican groups with Colombian cocaine suppliers and moved drugs into the United States. He was convicted in the 1985 kidnapping and murder of U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration agent Enrique “Kiki” Camarena and Mexican pilot Alfredo Zavala Avelar, and was serving consecutive 40- and 37-year sentences. The Guadalajara Cartel later split into regional groups, including the Sinaloa Cartel. Félix Gallardo’s family was expected to hold a small religious ceremony at the hospital, according to Jalisco security ministry spokesman Jorge Eduardo Montiel.
world.image_alt: Founder of Mexico’s Guadalajara Cartel dies in custody at 80

world.title: Shophouse fire on Thailand’s Phuket island kills 11, injures 16
world.summary: A fire tore through a commercial shophouse and nearby buildings in Patong on Thailand’s Phuket island early Monday, killing at least 11 people and injuring 16, police said. Firefighters took about two hours to control the blaze, which began in a building used by a vehicle-rental business near Patong Beach. Police said
world.content: A fire tore through a commercial shophouse and nearby buildings in Patong on Thailand’s Phuket island early Monday, killing at least 11 people and injuring 16, police said. Firefighters took about two hours to control the blaze, which began in a building used by a vehicle-rental business near Patong Beach. Police said no tourists were among the dead or injured; those injured included 15 Thai nationals and one person from Myanmar. The fire spread through connected commercial and residential buildings. Phuket Governor Chodnarin Koedsom said the rental shop stored about 100 motorcycles, as well as gas, engine oil, plastic materials and tires, which may have helped the flames and thick smoke spread. Officials have not established the cause, but initial investigations found that an electrical transformer near the building had exploded shortly before the fire. Authorities set up a temporary relief centre for residents displaced by the blaze, while rescue teams continued searching affected buildings and assisting people in critical condition. Police and forensic teams are examining the scene to determine how the fire started and spread.
world.image_alt: Shophouse fire on Thailand’s Phuket island kills 11, injures 16

world.title: ASEAN leaves South China Sea code unfinished, maintains Myanmar leaders’ summit ban
world.summary: Southeast Asian leaders at the Manila summit maintained a ban on Myanmar’s military-backed leaders attending ASEAN meetings unless the country shows “sustained and concrete progress” on a peace plan, while negotiations with China on a South China Sea code of conduct remained unfinished. The unresolved disputes will pas
world.content: Southeast Asian leaders at the Manila summit maintained a ban on Myanmar’s military-backed leaders attending ASEAN meetings unless the country shows “sustained and concrete progress” on a peace plan, while negotiations with China on a South China Sea code of conduct remained unfinished. The unresolved disputes will pass to Singapore when it takes over ASEAN’s rotating chairmanship in 2027. Chinese Premier Li Qiang told leaders on Monday that China and ASEAN should “stand united” against outside interference, citing more than $1 trillion in annual trade and more than $500 billion in cumulative two-way investment. Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto also apologized to Singapore and Malaysia for haze from months of forest and peatland fires. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi began his Manila visit on Monday ahead of ASEAN-India and East Asia summit meetings scheduled for Tuesday. U.S. President Donald Trump is due in Manila on Tuesday for meetings with ASEAN leaders and the Quad — the United States, India, Japan and Australia — before continuing to China.
world.image_alt: ASEAN leaves South China Sea code unfinished, maintains Myanmar leaders’ summit ban

world.title: Zelenskyy says Starshield restrictions threaten Ukraine’s winter energy defenses
world.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Sunday that speed restrictions on Starshield, SpaceX’s military satellite communications service, are disrupting communications for Ukrainian interceptor drones and could weaken defenses of energy infrastructure ahead of winter. He said the drones lose contact with operators
world.content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Sunday that speed restrictions on Starshield, SpaceX’s military satellite communications service, are disrupting communications for Ukrainian interceptor drones and could weaken defenses of energy infrastructure ahead of winter. He said the drones lose contact with operators above 161 kph (100 mph) along the front line and in Russian-occupied areas, preventing them from catching Russian Shahed attack drones. He directed Ukraine’s foreign and defense ministries and presidential office to press the United States and SpaceX to lift the limits. Responsibility remains disputed. SpaceX has denied imposing restrictions and cited technical problems, according to Ukrainian officials quoted by RFE/RL. SpaceX’s Elon Musk has said the U.S. government controls Starshield, while President Donald Trump has denied involvement in the limits. Zelenskyy has questioned whether the restrictions are technical and said they carry political implications for Ukraine’s occupied territory. Russia continues to attack Ukrainian infrastructure: a strike on Chornomorsk temporarily cut power to about 41,000 customers, and Zelenskyy said Russia launched more than 2,300 drones, 1,590 guided bombs and 15 missiles in the past week. Ukraine’s allies are preparing a Coalition of the Willing meeting, while the Ramstein group of countries supporting Ukraine’s defense is due to meet next week.
world.image_alt: Zelenskyy says Starshield restrictions threaten Ukraine’s winter energy defenses

world.title: Eisenkot demands Netanyahu quit as probe examines election-day arrests
world.summary: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot demanded on Nov. 15 that caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu leave office after a Channel 12 investigation alleged that Netanyahu’s chief of staff, Ido Norden, directed police to a former employee of the Prime Minister’s Office whose information led to the election-day ar
world.content: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot demanded on Nov. 15 that caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu leave office after a Channel 12 investigation alleged that Netanyahu’s chief of staff, Ido Norden, directed police to a former employee of the Prime Minister’s Office whose information led to the election-day arrests of three Arab Ra’am activists. Police and the attorney general’s office are examining whether the information was planted to bolster claims that Arab parties had stolen the Oct. 27 election. Police released all three activists without charges after finding the allegations unfounded; Netanyahu’s office called the report false and said Norden had passed on information as a citizen. Eisenkot called for an immediate investigation and said he would seek a commission of inquiry. Netanyahu’s Likud party accused him of incitement and defended the prime minister’s offer to discuss a unity government. The election left neither side with a majority in the 120-seat Knesset; Arab parties won 19 seats, and Ra’am and the Joint List have indicated support for Eisenkot. A separate Channel 12 report said Shin Bet chief David Zini sought authorization to wiretap five Arab lawmakers on election day, but the attorney general’s office rejected the request. The Shin Bet said its election-related investigation complied with legal authority and instructions from the Central Elections Committee chair.
world.image_alt: Eisenkot demands Netanyahu quit as probe examines election-day arrests

world.title: Czechs rally in Prague against proposed 15% public media cuts
world.summary: An estimated 350,000 to 450,000 people rallied in Prague on Nov. 15 against Prime Minister Andrej Babiš’s plan to replace household licence fees for Czech Television and Czech Radio with state-budget funding. Organizers from the Million Moments for Democracy civic group said the rally could be the country’s largest pro
world.content: An estimated 350,000 to 450,000 people rallied in Prague on Nov. 15 against Prime Minister Andrej Babiš’s plan to replace household licence fees for Czech Television and Czech Radio with state-budget funding. Organizers from the Million Moments for Democracy civic group said the rally could be the country’s largest protest since the 1989 Velvet Revolution. The proposal would cut the broadcasters’ budgets by about 15%, and critics say dependence on annual state allocations could expose editorial decisions to political pressure. Babiš’s government says the change will lower household costs and insists it does not seek to control programming. It also says broadcasters need to reduce spending. The bill cleared its first parliamentary reading in an overnight vote in October, prompting protests and a one-day strike by public-media staff on Nov. 3. The draft still faces further debate. Demonstrators called for its withdrawal and for safeguards to protect broadcaster independence.
world.image_alt: Czechs rally in Prague against proposed 15% public media cuts

world.title: China confirms Trump, Putin and Xi summit on nuclear arms, Iran
world.summary: China confirmed Monday that President Xi Jinping will host U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on Nov. 19 for their first three-way summit, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders’ meeting. The White House and Kremlin had already announced the me
world.content: China confirmed Monday that President Xi Jinping will host U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on Nov. 19 for their first three-way summit, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders’ meeting. The White House and Kremlin had already announced the meeting. U.S. officials say Trump wants to discuss nuclear arms reductions and the war with Iran; Washington says Russia’s war in Ukraine is not on the trilateral agenda. China’s Foreign Ministry gave no agenda details, while U.S. officials said they do not expect an agreement and described the talks as an opening conversation. The discussions follow the February expiration of New START, the last major U.S.-Russia nuclear arms-control treaty, which set binding limits on strategic arsenals. China has long argued that Washington and Moscow should cut their much larger arsenals before Beijing joins nuclear-reduction talks. The White House schedule lists the meeting at Kylin Villa resort for 2:30 p.m. local time on Nov. 19; Trump is also scheduled to have lunch with Xi.
world.image_alt: China confirms Trump, Putin and Xi summit on nuclear arms, Iran

business.title: Canada weighs Chinese auto investment if U.S. talks fail
business.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada could seek investment from Chinese, European or Japanese automakers if trade talks with President Donald Trump fail to preserve an integrated North American auto industry. He stressed that an agreement with Washington remains his priority. He spoke in Cambodia on Nov. 16
business.content: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada could seek investment from Chinese, European or Japanese automakers if trade talks with President Donald Trump fail to preserve an integrated North American auto industry. He stressed that an agreement with Washington remains his priority. He spoke in Cambodia on Nov. 16 before a planned Nov. 17 meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, where auto manufacturing is expected to be discussed. Carney said any Chinese investment must involve substantial Canadian manufacturing, meet labour standards and develop domestic supply chains that grow over time and include Canadian critical minerals, rather than rely solely on assembling imported parts. A January agreement cut Canada’s tariff on Chinese electric vehicles from 100% to 6.1%, initially allowing 49,000 imports a year in exchange for lower Chinese tariffs on Canadian farm goods. Carney said U.S. negotiations were making progress but differences remained. Canada has also threatened legal action against Stellantis after it shifted planned Jeep Compass production from Ontario to Illinois.
business.image_alt: Canada weighs Chinese auto investment if U.S. talks fail

business.title: US-led group signs pact to secure AI supply chains from China
business.summary: The United States and eight partners signed the San Francisco Declaration on the Secure Foundations of Enduring Prosperity, pledging to identify and protect artificial-intelligence technologies and supply chains viewed as vulnerable to China’s influence. Japan, Australia, Israel, the United Kingdom, South Korea, India,
business.content: The United States and eight partners signed the San Francisco Declaration on the Secure Foundations of Enduring Prosperity, pledging to identify and protect artificial-intelligence technologies and supply chains viewed as vulnerable to China’s influence. Japan, Australia, Israel, the United Kingdom, South Korea, India, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates joined the United States; Germany, Sweden, the Netherlands and the European Commission are expected to sign next week. The agreement is part of the US-led Pax Silica initiative and covers supply-chain risks involving semiconductors, critical minerals, energy infrastructure and other AI-related systems. Its signatories plan to form working groups to identify vulnerabilities, share information and explore investment hubs. US economic affairs official Jacob Helberg said AI supply chains cross borders, making their security a shared responsibility.
business.image_alt: US-led group signs pact to secure AI supply chains from China

business.title: AI forecasts point to job shifts as banks curb hiring
business.summary: Artificial intelligence is projected to create 10.6 million jobs worldwide and eliminate 8.9 million from 2025 to 2030, a net gain of about 1.7 million, according to Gartner. More than 20% of workers, or 435.5 million people, may need to adapt their tasks or roles. In banking, lenders are already automating routine wor
business.content: Artificial intelligence is projected to create 10.6 million jobs worldwide and eliminate 8.9 million from 2025 to 2030, a net gain of about 1.7 million, according to Gartner. More than 20% of workers, or 435.5 million people, may need to adapt their tasks or roles. In banking, lenders are already automating routine work, cutting some positions and restricting hiring, while evidence that AI is generating significant new revenue remains limited. German labor-market researchers found that employment among younger workers in AI-exposed jobs weakened relative to less-exposed roles, although they attributed much of the pressure to a weak economy. A Slovak forecast projects that new roles will partly offset AI-related job losses, while an aging workforce is expected to create a larger labor shortage. Banks and other employers are also seeking more AI, software and data expertise as routine entry-level work changes.
business.image_alt: AI forecasts point to job shifts as banks curb hiring

business.title: Bessent urges Nvidia to hire outside CEO, answer export-control questions
business.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged Nvidia’s board on Sunday to choose a chief executive from outside the company and demanded answers within 10 days about whether Nvidia complied with U.S. restrictions on advanced chip exports to China. The demand follows Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang’s Nov. 12 resignation af
business.content: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged Nvidia’s board on Sunday to choose a chief executive from outside the company and demanded answers within 10 days about whether Nvidia complied with U.S. restrictions on advanced chip exports to China. The demand follows Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang’s Nov. 12 resignation after revelations about personal relationships, including one with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based data-center company Megaspeed whom U.S. officials suspect of links to Chinese intelligence. The espionage allegation has not been established, and Megaspeed denies wrongdoing. The export-control inquiry centers on suspicions that shell companies and Megaspeed helped route restricted Nvidia processors to Chinese buyers. Bessent questioned whether Nvidia ignored warning signs to increase revenue. Nvidia says it complies with U.S. export laws, while Megaspeed says it has hired outside counsel to review its operations. The U.S. Justice Department is investigating Megaspeed, and congressional committees are seeking testimony from Huang and other Nvidia officials. Nvidia is due to report quarterly results Tuesday, Nov. 17, under interim chief executive Colette Kress. The board has not named a permanent successor; some Silicon Valley allies are pressing for Huang’s return, while Bessent is calling for an outside hire.
business.image_alt: Bessent urges Nvidia to hire outside CEO, answer export-control questions

business.title: FAA ground stop follows network upgrade as Duffy seeks $50 billion
business.summary: A Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) network failure grounded nearly all departing U.S. flights for more than four hours on Nov. 13, after a routine upgrade involving a router at an Arkansas facility disrupted communications and radar data. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said investigators were examining router
business.content: A Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) network failure grounded nearly all departing U.S. flights for more than four hours on Nov. 13, after a routine upgrade involving a router at an Arkansas facility disrupted communications and radar data. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said investigators were examining routers from Arkansas and Texas, but had not determined whether the failure came from installation error or faulty equipment; officials said they saw no evidence of a cyberattack. The stoppage triggered thousands of cancellations and delays over the weekend as airlines repositioned aircraft and crews. President Donald Trump blamed the Biden administration and urged Congress to fund a broader overhaul. Duffy has called for $50 billion, saying last year’s $12.5 billion FAA allocation does not cover a new telecommunications network and airspace-management software. The funding request faces resistance from senior congressional Democrats, who say much of the existing allocation remains unspent. Duffy said the FAA disabled the routers’ ability to broadcast data while the investigation continues, and projected that a replacement network could be completed by the end of 2028 or early 2029 if Congress provides the money.
business.image_alt: FAA ground stop follows network upgrade as Duffy seeks $50 billion

business.title: Anthropic IPO draws nearly sevenfold demand ahead of Nasdaq debut
business.summary: Anthropic’s planned stock-market debut has drawn orders for nearly seven times the shares available, as the maker of Claude prepares to list on Nasdaq on Nov. 19. The company is offering 825 million shares at $70 to $78 apiece, a range that implies a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion; a separate private placement could
business.content: Anthropic’s planned stock-market debut has drawn orders for nearly seven times the shares available, as the maker of Claude prepares to list on Nasdaq on Nov. 19. The company is offering 825 million shares at $70 to $78 apiece, a range that implies a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion; a separate private placement could bring the total raised by Anthropic and its backers to about $90 billion. Anthropic disclosed more than $900 billion in spending commitments, reported a $104 billion net loss in the first nine months of 2026 and held $132 billion in cash and short-term investments, CNBC reported. The valuation target is below the $2 trillion discussed by shareholders in August, while quarterly revenue growth slowed in the third quarter. Anthropic plans to debut on Nasdaq on Nov. 19.
business.image_alt: Anthropic IPO draws nearly sevenfold demand ahead of Nasdaq debut

business.title: Trump seeks Asia trade deals as US-China truce nears expiry
business.summary: President Donald Trump is using his Asia trip to pursue commercial agreements, including a planned trade deal with Thailand in Manila. The White House says he will sign that deal and other commercial agreements. In Shenzhen, Trump is expected to focus on trade issues with China as the two countries prepare for talks ah
business.content: President Donald Trump is using his Asia trip to pursue commercial agreements, including a planned trade deal with Thailand in Manila. The White House says he will sign that deal and other commercial agreements. In Shenzhen, Trump is expected to focus on trade issues with China as the two countries prepare for talks ahead of their trade truce’s Jan. 10, 2027, expiration. Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are scheduled to hold their first trilateral meeting in Shenzhen on Nov. 19, with nuclear weapons and Iran expected to be the focus. Trump is also expected to address trade issues during his China visit. Economists say the discussions could test whether the existing truce can be extended or replaced with a longer-term framework; the U.S. is pressing China to fulfill commitments made under the agreement. U.S. scrutiny of advanced-chip exports has grown after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned. Officials have discussed closing loopholes that allow Chinese businesses to obtain advanced U.S. chips, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the key question is whether Nvidia complied with export rules.
business.image_alt: Trump seeks Asia trade deals as US-China truce nears expiry

business.title: China’s October retail, factory output and investment data miss forecasts as growth cools
business.summary: China’s economic momentum weakened in October, with retail sales up just 0.4% from a year earlier, industrial output growth slowing to 4.8% and fixed-asset investment down 8.1% in the first 10 months, according to data released Monday. Each measure missed economists’ forecasts; September retail sales and industrial out
business.content: China’s economic momentum weakened in October, with retail sales up just 0.4% from a year earlier, industrial output growth slowing to 4.8% and fixed-asset investment down 8.1% in the first 10 months, according to data released Monday. Each measure missed economists’ forecasts; September retail sales and industrial output had risen 1.1% and 5.5%, respectively. The property downturn has eroded household wealth, while property investment fell 21.6% in January-October. Goods exports rose 35.2% in October, and China’s trade surplus passed $1 trillion by that month. Analysts warn that export-led growth is vulnerable to a pullback in global demand, including for artificial intelligence (AI) products. Third-quarter gross domestic product grew 4.5% year over year, within Beijing’s 4.5%-5% target for 2026. ANZ senior China strategist Zhaopeng Xing expects no new stimulus measures for the rest of this year, while ING chief economist for Greater China Lynn Song says domestic demand would benefit from more policy support.
business.image_alt: China’s October retail, factory output and investment data miss forecasts as growth cools

science.title: COP31 nations split over 1.5°C goal as threshold nears
science.summary: Halfway through the COP31 climate negotiations in Antalya, countries are divided over whether to keep the 1.5°C warming limit as a central goal after the United Nations said in September that crossing it was imminent and unavoidable. Global temperatures have risen about 1.4°C above pre-industrial levels. Some countries
science.content: Halfway through the COP31 climate negotiations in Antalya, countries are divided over whether to keep the 1.5°C warming limit as a central goal after the United Nations said in September that crossing it was imminent and unavoidable. Global temperatures have risen about 1.4°C above pre-industrial levels. Some countries want the summit’s final decision to reaffirm 1.5°C as the “right goal” and call for temperatures to return below that limit as soon as possible. Other negotiators, including members of the Arab Group and Like-Minded Developing Countries, are pushing to weaken or remove references to the target. Scientists say reversing an overshoot would require sharp emissions cuts and large-scale carbon removal over decades; University of Exeter climate scientist Pierre Friedlingstein described that prospect as “extremely ambitious”.
science.image_alt: COP31 nations split over 1.5°C goal as threshold nears

science.title: Powerful El Niño may rival 1997 event, shaping winter weather
science.summary: The 2026 El Niño has reached the top of the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s (NOAA) intensity scale, and NASA researchers say satellite measurements show it could rival or exceed the 1997-98 event. The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) expects it to strengthen until a December peak and says
science.content: The 2026 El Niño has reached the top of the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s (NOAA) intensity scale, and NASA researchers say satellite measurements show it could rival or exceed the 1997-98 event. The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) expects it to strengthen until a December peak and says it is nearly certain to persist through February 2027. The event is expected to alter global temperatures and rainfall, but researchers caution that similar ocean patterns do not guarantee identical weather. NOAA’s winter outlook favors warmer conditions across much of the northern United States and wetter-than-average conditions in parts of the South and East. The WMO also reports that drought is affecting fields, harvests and livestock in Central America, while disrupted monsoon rains are threatening crops in India.
science.image_alt: Powerful El Niño may rival 1997 event, shaping winter weather

science.title: Climate scientists warn powerful El Niño could intensify 2026 disasters
science.summary: Climate officials warn that El Niño could be exceptionally strong and intensify weather extremes as the COP31 climate summit meets in Antalya. It is expected to peak in December and affect conditions through 2027. The Guardian describes it as the strongest in at least 1,000 years, while Turkish climate researcher Doğuk
science.content: Climate officials warn that El Niño could be exceptionally strong and intensify weather extremes as the COP31 climate summit meets in Antalya. It is expected to peak in December and affect conditions through 2027. The Guardian describes it as the strongest in at least 1,000 years, while Turkish climate researcher Doğukan Doğu Yavaşlı said some models approach a “super El Niño” scenario. The U.N. refugee agency projects up to 3 million displacements across Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan and Uganda, while maize production in Kenya is already falling by 40%. Drought has also hit the rainfall-dependent Marshall Islands, which declared a state of emergency.
science.image_alt: Climate scientists warn powerful El Niño could intensify 2026 disasters

science.title: NASA calls for public Morse-code tribute before Voyager 1 milestone
science.summary: NASA is asking people to flash Voyager 1’s call sign in Morse code after sunset on Nov. 17, ahead of the probe’s expected arrival one light-day from Earth on Nov. 18. It would be the first human-made object to reach that distance. A radio message would take 24 hours each way, so receiving a reply would take about two d
science.content: NASA is asking people to flash Voyager 1’s call sign in Morse code after sunset on Nov. 17, ahead of the probe’s expected arrival one light-day from Earth on Nov. 18. It would be the first human-made object to reach that distance. A radio message would take 24 hours each way, so receiving a reply would take about two days. Launched in 1977, Voyager 1 continues to return science and engineering data from interstellar space. Reaching one light-day does not mark its departure from the solar system: the spacecraft remains within the Sun’s gravitational reach and is still about 300 years from the inner edge of the Oort Cloud, according to NASA estimates cited by planetary scientist Pascal Lee.
science.image_alt: NASA calls for public Morse-code tribute before Voyager 1 milestone

science.title: 6,000-year-old tooth tracks dietary shift as farming reached Denmark
science.summary: A tooth from Rødhals Man, a hunter-gatherer buried on Denmark’s Sejerø island nearly 6,000 years ago, records a shift from seafood in childhood toward more land-based food in adolescence and adulthood as farming reached the islands. Researchers used chemical signatures in successive layers of a premolar to reconstruct
science.content: A tooth from Rødhals Man, a hunter-gatherer buried on Denmark’s Sejerø island nearly 6,000 years ago, records a shift from seafood in childhood toward more land-based food in adolescence and adulthood as farming reached the islands. Researchers used chemical signatures in successive layers of a premolar to reconstruct his dietary changes. They say the evidence makes him one of the rare individuals known to have lived through the transition. His ancestry was that of the local forager population, while his diet suggests contact with the incoming farming way of life. The chemistry cannot establish whether his land-based food came directly from farms. But researchers favor food from, or proximity to, farming communities because his diet lacked the freshwater fish typical of inland foragers.
science.image_alt: 6,000-year-old tooth tracks dietary shift as farming reached Denmark

science.title: Astronomers trace eight-minute radio pulses to rare Sun-like star pair
science.summary: Astronomers have traced radio bursts repeating every 7.9 minutes to GPM J071507−114153, a binary system more than 5,000 light-years away. The system pairs a rapidly spinning white dwarf with a G-type star similar to the Sun. It is the first long-period radio transient identified with a Sun-like companion; previously id
science.content: Astronomers have traced radio bursts repeating every 7.9 minutes to GPM J071507−114153, a binary system more than 5,000 light-years away. The system pairs a rapidly spinning white dwarf with a G-type star similar to the Sun. It is the first long-period radio transient identified with a Sun-like companion; previously identified systems of this kind involved cooler, smaller red dwarfs. The observations allowed researchers to track the white dwarf around its companion and locate the likely source of the pulses near, or possibly on, the white dwarf. The team also detected magnetic activity on the Sun-like star. The findings, based on more than 100 hours of radio observations and optical data, were published in Nature Astronomy. The mechanism that produces these intermittent signals remains unexplained, and researchers say further observations are needed.
science.image_alt: Astronomers trace eight-minute radio pulses to rare Sun-like star pair

science.title: Leonid meteor shower peaks this week, with fewer than three meteors an hour forecast
science.summary: The annual Leonid meteor shower is expected to peak on the night of Nov. 16-17, though forecasts differ on the timing. Visibility estimates range from fewer than three meteors an hour to 10-15 under ideal dark skies. The shower occurs as Earth crosses dust and debris shed by comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle; the particles enter
science.content: The annual Leonid meteor shower is expected to peak on the night of Nov. 16-17, though forecasts differ on the timing. Visibility estimates range from fewer than three meteors an hour to 10-15 under ideal dark skies. The shower occurs as Earth crosses dust and debris shed by comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle; the particles enter the atmosphere at about 44 miles per second, producing fast, sometimes bright streaks. For the best chance of seeing meteors, observers should look after midnight from a dark, open location, watch a broad area of sky and give their eyes time to adjust; no telescope is needed. Moonlight may hide fainter meteors, while clouds and artificial lights can further reduce visibility. NASA’s peak estimate for East Coast viewers is Monday night into Tuesday, while other forecasts put peak activity on Nov. 17-18.
science.image_alt: Leonid meteor shower peaks this week, with fewer than three meteors an hour forecast

science.title: Chinese researchers identify giant fungus with 65-million-year lineage
science.summary: Researchers at the Kunming Institute of Botany in China identified a giant fungus, Dianjunus rex, in Yunnan Province. Its above-ground fruiting bodies can reach 20 inches and weigh nearly 5 pounds. A DNA-based molecular-clock analysis estimated that the lineage diverged from other species about 65 million years ago, ar
science.content: Researchers at the Kunming Institute of Botany in China identified a giant fungus, Dianjunus rex, in Yunnan Province. Its above-ground fruiting bodies can reach 20 inches and weigh nearly 5 pounds. A DNA-based molecular-clock analysis estimated that the lineage diverged from other species about 65 million years ago, around the end of the Cretaceous period. The team found the fungus in the Nanban tropical rainforest, growing near the roots of dying trees. Genetic analysis showed that it has about half as many decomposition-related genes as some close relatives. Lead author Indunil C. Senanayake, an associate professor at the institute, suggested it may live inside healthy trees before feeding on dead plant material, but described the idea as a theory.

sports.title: Mary Earps saves London City point as Arsenal extend home-draw run

sports.content: London City Lionesses goalkeeper Mary Earps made eight saves as her side drew 1-1 with Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium on Sunday, leaving Arsenal without a home Women’s Super League win in five matches there this season. Frida Maanum put Arsenal ahead in the 10th minute, but Isobel Goodwin equalised 98 seconds later. Earps then kept out several Arsenal efforts, tipping one from Maanum onto the crossbar. The draw leaves London City third on 20 points and Arsenal sixth on 14, six points behind the final Champions League qualification place. London City earned their first points against Arsenal, who had won all seven previous meetings. Arsenal next host OL Lyonnes in the Women’s Champions League on Thursday, while London City are due to play Brighton in the Subway Players’ Cup on Wednesday.

sports.title: Kirk Cousins leads Vikings past Packers in emotional return
sports.summary: The Minnesota Vikings beat the Green Bay Packers 30-10 in Green Bay on Sunday as quarterback Kirk Cousins threw two touchdown passes in his first game back with Minnesota since the Las Vegas Raiders traded him Tuesday. sports.content: The Minnesota Vikings beat the Green Bay Packers 30-10 in Green Bay on Sunday as quarterback Kirk Cousins threw two touchdown passes in his first game back with Minnesota since the Las Vegas Raiders traded him Tuesday. Cousins completed 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards with one interception. He returned at Lambeau Field, where he tore his Achilles tendon in his final Vikings game in 2023. The win ended Minnesota’s two-game losing streak and lifted the Vikings to 7-2, tied with the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears atop the NFC North. Minnesota’s defense recorded eight sacks and forced four turnovers, while Cousins led an offense that had struggled in previous games. Cousins said the return was emotional after what he called a difficult three years since the injury. Minnesota next faces the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City the following Sunday.

sports.title: Detroit Lions beat Patriots 35-10 as St. Brown stars in Germany
sports.summary: The Detroit Lions beat the New England Patriots 35-10 in Munich on Sunday as wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown scored twice in his first game in Germany and running back Jahmyr Gibbs added two touchdowns. Detroit improved to 7-2 with its fifth straight win; New England fell to 5-5 after quarterback Drake Maye left early
sports.content: The Detroit Lions beat the New England Patriots 35-10 in Munich on Sunday as wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown scored twice in his first game in Germany and running back Jahmyr Gibbs added two touchdowns. Detroit improved to 7-2 with its fifth straight win; New England fell to 5-5 after quarterback Drake Maye left early with an ankle injury. St. Brown, whose mother is German, scored on a 56-yard reception and added a touchdown catch in the third quarter. Gibbs gained 252 yards from scrimmage, while quarterback Jared Goff threw for 303 yards and three touchdowns. St. Brown said the trip and victory in front of German fans felt like a dream come true. Detroit edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson hurt his knee while celebrating a first-quarter sack, and Lions coach Dan Campbell said the team would know more after returning to the United States. Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said Maye would undergo further tests. New England enters its bye week after losing three of its past four games.

sports.title: Former Australia bowler backs claim whole team knew about 2018 ball-tampering
sports.summary: Former Australia fast bowler Chadd Sayers has backed ex-opener Usman Khawaja’s claim that the whole team knew about ball-tampering during the 2018 South Africa tour, saying players used sandpaper in two Tests and discussed it in the dressing room. Sayers, who was 12th man at Cape Town, also said he was handed the sandp
sports.content: Former Australia fast bowler Chadd Sayers has backed ex-opener Usman Khawaja’s claim that the whole team knew about ball-tampering during the 2018 South Africa tour, saying players used sandpaper in two Tests and discussed it in the dressing room. Sayers, who was 12th man at Cape Town, also said he was handed the sandpaper to take off the field during the previous Test. Current Australia captain Pat Cummins has rejected Khawaja’s account as “100 per cent wrong,” saying he did not know about the plan. Khawaja’s autobiography has reopened debate over the scandal and the penalties imposed on then-captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner and Cameron Bancroft. Warner has also supported Khawaja, while governing body Cricket Australia says it will not reopen its investigation. Former fast bowler Jason Gillespie has urged it to address public questions about its findings. Khawaja says any damage to his relationship with Cricket Australia would be a small price to pay for speaking up, but acknowledged the personal and family costs.

sports.content: England beat Australia by 135 runs in Adelaide on Sunday, November 15, levelling their three-match one-day international series at 1-1 after losing the opener in Perth. Tom Banton’s 121 from 99 balls helped England post 355 for six, their highest ODI total in Australia, before Gus Atkinson took a career-best four for 28 as Australia were bowled out for 220. Atkinson and new-ball partner Sonny Baker helped reduce Australia to 29 for four inside seven overs. Matt Renshaw and Cameron Green then added 98 runs, but Liam Dawson dismissed both, and Sam Curran took two wickets in successive deliveries. England’s win was their biggest ODI victory by runs in Australia. The teams meet in Hobart on Wednesday, November 18, for the series decider. Both sides are using the tour to prepare for the 2027 World Cup in South Africa.

sports.title: Week 10 wins lift Vikings, Bengals and Browns in NFL playoff races
sports.summary: The Minnesota Vikings beat Green Bay 30-10, the Cincinnati Bengals defeated Pittsburgh 38-18 and the Cleveland Browns rallied from 17 points down to beat Houston 27-24 in Sunday’s NFL games. sports.content: The Minnesota Vikings beat Green Bay 30-10, the Cincinnati Bengals defeated Pittsburgh 38-18 and the Cleveland Browns rallied from 17 points down to beat Houston 27-24 in Sunday’s NFL games. The Vikings’ win came in quarterback Kirk Cousins’ first game back with Minnesota, five days after the team acquired him from the Las Vegas Raiders. The Bengals took sole possession of the AFC North lead, while the Browns moved into the AFC’s final projected playoff spot. Detroit stayed level with Minnesota and Chicago atop the NFC North by beating New England 35-10 in Munich, but defensive end Aidan Hutchinson suffered a serious-looking knee injury. The San Francisco 49ers remained the NFC’s top seed after a 46-40 win over Dallas, while Buffalo improved to 8-1 by beating the Jets. The Vikings visit the 49ers next week in Mexico City.

sports.content: The Seattle Seahawks beat the Las Vegas Raiders 21-13 on Sunday, spoiling rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza’s first NFL start. The No. 1 overall draft pick and former Heisman Trophy winner opened with a 10-yard rushing touchdown but finished 17 of 29 for 143 yards and was sacked six times. Seattle quarterback Drew Lock threw for 240 yards and two touchdowns, including a 71-yard score to receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba. The Raiders’ offense stalled after tight end Brock Bowers left with an ankle injury, and Las Vegas managed only 27 yards in the second half. Mendoza said the game exposed areas he needs to improve; Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak also took responsibility for not helping the rookie more after halftime. Seattle enters its bye at 6-4, while the Raiders travel to Denver to face the Broncos next week.

sports.summary: World No. 1 Alexander Zverev started his ATP Finals title bid in Turin on Sunday with a 6-4, 6-4 win over 20-year-old Spanish debutant Rafael Jodar. The German, who won his first two Grand Slam titles this year, broke once in each set and saved two break points while serving out the first set. It was his first victory
sports.content: World No. 1 Alexander Zverev started his ATP Finals title bid in Turin on Sunday with a 6-4, 6-4 win over 20-year-old Spanish debutant Rafael Jodar. The German, who won his first two Grand Slam titles this year, broke once in each set and saved two break points while serving out the first set. It was his first victory since taking the top ranking after an opening-match loss at the Paris Masters. In the same group, American Ben Shelton beat France’s Arthur Fils 6-2, 3-6, 6-3 for his first win at the season-ending tournament after losing all three matches on his debut last year. The eight-player event runs through November 22, with the top two in each round-robin group advancing to the semifinals. Zverev’s next group match is against Shelton on Tuesday, while Carlos Alcaraz begins his campaign against Frances Tiafoe on Monday.
